title: Freelance time management: visualize goals, prioritize, schedule, cut distractions, say no
summary: Ross Jenkins, founder of DigitalME, gives five practical time management habits for freelancers. He covers goal visualization, ranking work by value and urgency, logging tasks on a calendar, removing distractions, and refusing work to avoid burnout. The advice is generic but reflects a stability-over-volume mindset.

principles.text: Keep your goal visible daily so your time decisions orient toward it.
principles.quote: Reading the same message with your main goal every morning will make your time management oriented towards achieving it.

principles.text: Rank work by value or urgency; do critical tasks first and archive the rest.
principles.quote: Activities that aren’t important or urgent can be deleted or archived indefinitely until all others have been completed.

principles.text: Log every task with details, deadlines and status on a calendar to measure productivity.
principles.quote: Keeping a log of your tasks will help you measure your productivity.

principles.text: Remove distractions by using a dedicated workspace and blocking social media during work hours.
principles.quote: it’s a good practice to choose a workplace exclusively for your freelance activities so that it is impossible for you to try to do something different.

principles.text: Overloading yourself with jobs causes missed deadlines and damages client relationships.
principles.quote: It’s essential to keep yourself mentally healthy by only taking the jobs you can handle.

principles.text: Aim for stable long-term work rather than grabbing every job, and learn to say no.
principles.quote: A necessary skill to succeed in freelancing is the ability to reject jobs when you know you don’t have the time to do them.
